summary: Macon County lookout site in Nantahala National Forest; tower list marks it lookout no tower; only a <1926 marker and trail listings found.

access.note: Hiking routes on national forest land reach the site: a Bartram Trail route and an Appalachian Trail access trail from FS 69B. No source describes a closure or permit.

visit.trail_note: Reached by a Bartram Trail route and by an Appalachian Trail access trail from FS 69B.

evidence.supports: Listed under the Nantahala National Forest
The only date on the page is the marker <1926, with no further detail
Tower list places Winespring Bald at 35.17361, -83.58111 in Macon County and marks it lookout no tower
The list names Peter Barr's book as a reference
The referenced book is Hiking North Carolina's Lookout Towers
Bartram Trail route lists Wayah Bald Fire Tower and Wine Spring Bald as stops
evidence.quote: Wayah Bald Fire Tower , Wine Spring Bald , Wine Spring Campsite

evidence.supports: Gaia GPS spells the route name Wine Spring Bald
evidence.quote: Wine Spring Bald via Bartram Trail

evidence.supports: Carolina Mountain Club lists an Appalachian Trail route using a Wine Spring Bald access trail from FS 69B
evidence.quote: Appalachian Trail via Wine Spring Bald access trail from FS 69B

sources.title: Wine Spring Bald via Bartram Trail

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts and tnlandforms spell it Winespring Bald; Gaia GPS and the Carolina Mountain Club spell it Wine Spring Bald. The record keeps Winespring Bald, the spelling in the tower lists.

notes_for_editor: Very thin. Sources: a Forest Lookouts page with only a <1926 marker and no explanation; a tower list that marks the site lookout no tower and names Peter Barr's book (not read); two trail listings. No build date, builder, design, staffing, fire history or current structure found. The <1926 marker is quoted as printed; it may mean a date before 1926, but the page does not say so. The FFLOS and NHLR caches hold no entry for this site, and a live firetower.org fetch failed with a connection reset and was not retried. Possible next step: Peter Barr's book or NC Forest Service photo records. Access level public is inferred from trail listings on national forest land.
